## Anomaly
{"kind": "balance", "system": "rebirth", "title": "Rebirth cost and progress are inconsistent", "expected": "Rebirth needs a fixed threshold. The button shows true progress, fires only at 100%, and denial gives clear feedback. A rebirth resets cash and unlocks.", "observed": "Round 1 cost is $5000 and round 2 is $10.0K, with a stray 'REBIRTH $5000 (99%)' label in round 2 coverage. In round 2 rebirths=1, yet pressed buttons at 3%, 4% and 12% read as fired=true. rebirth_denied is 3 in round 1 and 5 in round 2, with little feedback. The judge also found an implausibly huge TotalEarned value. Cost may have changed after the rebirth, but the digest cannot confirm that.", "severity": "medium"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The server's rebirth count and the replicated leaderstats.Rebirths value diverge. RebirthService.tryRebirth increments its private s.rebirths and only writes `s.stat.Value` if `s.stat` is set. In the playtest `s.stat` was never bound to the player's real leaderstats.Rebirths IntValue. That value is created elsewhere (Game/DataService, and LeaderboardService.ensureValue), so it stayed 0. The server therefore moved on to the round-2 cost of $10000 and the x1.5 multiplier, while the client still derives the cost and progress from leaderstats.Rebirths (still 0). The button keeps showing 'REBIRTH $5000 (n%)' with percentages computed against the stale $5000 threshold. Presses are then judged against a different threshold than the server's, so denials in round 2 ('Need $10000...') look unexplained. The leaderboard also shows R0. This is a game bug, not a testing artefact. The huge TotalEarned is a side effect: the LeaderboardService counts every positive Cash delta, including the direct cash writes, so it was not the cause of the cost mismatch.", "file": "ServerScriptService/RebirthService.luau", "evidence": "Client probe at start: Rebirths=0, button 'REBIRTH $5000 (1%)'. Server probe after tryRebirth at $5000: getRebirths=1, RebirthMult=1.5, but leaderstats.Rebirths.Value=0. Client probe afterwards: leaderstats Rebirths=0, button still 'REBIRTH $5000 (0%)', although RebirthConfig.costFor(1)=10000, which is also the cost the server enforces in the denial message.", 

Probe (Client): Read the rebirth button text, leaderstats and attributes at the start to see how progress is displayed
```luau
local p=game.Players.LocalPlayer
local gui=p.PlayerGui:FindFirstChild("RebirthGui")
local b=gui and gui:FindFirstChild("RebirthButton")
local ls=p:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
local t={}
if ls then for _,c in ls:GetChildren() do t[c.Name]=c.Value end end
return game:GetService("HttpService"):JSONEncode({btn=b and b.Text,ls=t,attrs=p:GetAttributes()})
```
Result: {"attrs":{"PlotIndex":1,"RebirthMult":1,"StartCashGranted":true,"NextGoalCost":10,"TotalEarned":80,"TutorialText":"Step on the glowing green pad!","TutorialNonce":4,"NextGoalName":"Dropper 2","TutorialStep":3},"ls":{"Rebirths":0,"Cash":80},"btn":"REBIRTH $5000 (1%)"}

Probe (Server): Trigger a real rebirth at 5000 cash, then inspect state; next read client button text to check cost/progress after rebirth
```luau
local p=game.Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local RS=require(game.ServerScriptService.RebirthService)
p.leaderstats.Cash.Value=5000
RS.tryRebirth(p)
task.wait(1)
return game:GetService('HttpService'):JSONEncode({rb=RS.getRebirths(p),stat=p.leaderstats.Rebirths.Value,cash=p.leaderstats.Cash.Value,attrs=p:GetAttributes()})
```
Result: {"attrs":{"PlotIndex":1,"RebirthMult":1.5,"StartCashGranted":true,"NextGoalCost":10,"TutorialStep":3,"TutorialText":"Step on the glowing green pad!","TutorialNonce":5,"NextGoalName":"Dropper 2","TotalEarned":5008},"stat":0,"rb":1,"cash":8}

Probe (Client): Check button text, rebirth count and cash on the client after the rebirth. The server probe showed stat=0 even though rb=1, so the leaderstat may not be updating.
```luau
local p=game.Players.LocalPlayer
local b=p.PlayerGui.RebirthGui:FindFirstChild("RebirthButton")
local ls=p.leaderstats
local t={}
for _,c in ls:GetChildren() do t[c.Name]=c.Value end
return game:GetService("HttpService"):JSONEncode({btn=b.Text,ls=t,cash=ls.Cash.Value,attrs=p:GetAttributes()})
```

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

## Example checks
```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```

-- check: Buying an item without enough cash keeps the cash and grants nothing
-- covers: anomaly: shop sells items to players who cannot afford them
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

if not p then error("setup: no player") end

if owns then owns:Destroy() end
cash.Value = oldCash

         detail = "buy returned " .. tostring(bought) .. ", cash 3 -> " .. after .. ", owns " .. tostring(owns ~= nil) }

-- check: After a successful rebirth, the replicated leaderstats.Rebirths value equals the server's rebirth count
-- covers: anomaly: Rebirth cost and progress are inconsistent
-- consumer: ServerScriptService/LeaderboardService.server.luau:214
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]

while not p and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do

end

local ls = forge.waitFor(function() return p:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") end, 10)
if not ls then error("setup: no leaderstats") end
local cash = ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
local stat = ls:FindFirstChild("Rebirths")
if not cash then error("setup: no leaderstats.Cash") end
if not stat then error("setup: no leaderstats.Rebirths") end

local RS = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("RebirthService"))
local RC = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("RebirthConfig"))

	cash.Value = RC.costFor(RS.getRebirths(p))
